October 30, 2026

Senator briefed on Iran war plan calls it insane as Trump weighs post-midterm strikes

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

Sen. Chris Murphy said that in a classified briefing he was given a fairly detailed account of what renewed military operations against Iran would look like, described to lawmakers as a short-duration campaign. Murphy said the plan would lead to devastating escalation, a prolonging of the war and the likely destruction of the United States' commitment to the rule of law, pointing to open reporting that civilian infrastructure may be among the targets. Adm. Brad Cooper of Central Command briefed President Trump at the White House alongside Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Gen. Dan Caine, and officials have told Gulf states to prepare for a possible short, intense campaign after the midterm elections. No final decision has been announced.

US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves for first time since Korean War

tags: defence, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

The US Army has begun training soldiers to bury fellow troops in temporary mass graves, an exercise it says it has not conducted on a large scale since the Korean War. Soldiers from the 3rd Corps Sustainment Command and the 20th Engineer Brigade at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, worked with military chaplains and used diggers and excavators to test how bodies could be preserved intact until identification and repatriation. Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Rood said the exercise was a scientific, field-tested approach to managing the fallen in a high-intensity conflict, adding that if the country went to war tomorrow the military would otherwise be improvising. The training is intended to prepare for a scenario with a high number of casualties.

Pentagon fires three-star general and refers him for prosecution over alleged leaks

tags: defence, legal
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, who oversaw military planning for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, over allegations that he leaked classified information to journalists about the Iran war, the Russia-Ukraine conflict and other matters. A Pentagon official said Sylvia failed three polygraph tests, and spokesman Sean Parnell said the department took necessary personnel action to protect sensitive information and referred the case to the Justice Department for potential further legal action. President Trump said officials are very much looking for leakers and that Sylvia would have long-term problems. The dismissal follows several other high-ranking military departures under Hegseth, including three aides fired during an earlier leak investigation.

Binance says $6.3 billion stolen in largest crypto theft on record

tags: markets, tech
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Binance said roughly $6.3 billion was taken from the exchange in a security incident and halted all deposits and withdrawals, saying about $3 billion has been frozen and that it will cover all losses. Early findings indicate a hacker made unauthorised transactions after gaining access to a compromised engineer's laptop, and blockchain intelligence firm TRM assessed with high confidence that North Korean hacking unit TraderTraitor was responsible. Bitcoin fell 5% after the breach, dropping below $77,000. The theft exceeds the previous record, a $1.5 billion heist attributed to North Korea's Lazarus Group, and comes after Binance pleaded guilty in 2023 to anti-money-laundering violations and paid $4.3 billion in penalties; founder Changpeng Zhao, who served four months in prison, was later pardoned by President Trump.

California judge refuses federal demand to set aside 20,000 ballots

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal judge rejected the Trump administration's request that California sequester 20,000 ballots over claims of non-citizen voting, writing that never before in American history has the federal government on the eve of an election sought to coerce state and local governments to abandon their own constitutional procedures. Gov. Gavin Newsom responded to plans to send federal election monitors from agencies including the Bureau of Prisons and the DEA by making the seizure of ballots a felony in California. The state is also pre-deploying lawyers to battleground districts to monitor vote counting and the federal monitors themselves.

Trump cancels then reinstates weekend rallies days before midterms

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

President Trump cancelled scheduled rallies in Kansas and Iowa in the final weekend before Election Day, opting for telephone rallies, before the White House confirmed hours later that he would travel to both states on Sunday after all. The reversal followed new polling, including surveys from Emerson and the Washington Post showing Democrats leading in Kansas by several points and by nine points respectively. Vice President JD Vance also cancelled a trip to Minnesota. Asked by a Reuters reporter why the Kansas rally had been called off, Trump said the reporter was out of shape, disgusting and sick.

Putin says Russia is ready for war with Europe but does not want one

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow is prepared for a war with Europe but does not seek one, warning that if things go too far there will be no winners at all. Speaking after hosting a summit, he defended his calls this week with Finland and Norway. He also warned against any blocking of Baltic navigation, saying Russia would respond to any challenge.

Zelensky says Russia is preparing new ballistic missile strikes

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian intelligence indicates Russia is preparing new ballistic missile strikes, and renewed his request for Patriot missiles. Ukraine's naval forces said strikes the same day destroyed two Russian Su-34 fighter-bombers at a base in the Volgograd region, along with an Iskander launch site.

Dockworkers at more than 100 ports to strike over arms shipments

tags: politics, war
sources: @groundnews

Dockworkers in 22 countries plan to strike Friday against weapons shipments moving through commercial ports, with more than 25 unions across 113 ports taking part. Organisers estimate the action could disrupt more than 40% of Mediterranean cargo and over $2 billion in freight, affecting hubs in Germany, France, Spain, Greece, Morocco and India. Greek ferry services face cancellations and Italian unions have called a 24-hour general strike with demonstrations in more than 40 cities. The unions are demanding that ports stop facilitating arms shipments to conflict zones, though officials at some ports anticipate limited disruption.

Leaked NYPD policy would route ICE activity locations to City Hall

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

ICE officers in New York City have obtained an internal NYPD policy requiring the department to notify City Hall of the locations of day-to-day ICE activity, information that would then become publicly available under legal mandate. Enforcement and Removal Operations personnel speaking anonymously said the change would significantly affect operations in the New York metropolitan area, with one officer describing more than 20 protesters disrupting an early-morning operation and blocking vehicles. The policy comes as Mayor Zohran Mamdani continues to enact measures restricting federal immigration enforcement and strengthening the city's sanctuary status.

Congress asks Trump to preserve records of AI chatbot use in official decisions

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

The ranking members of the House Oversight and Judiciary Committees sent a letter to President Trump asking him to preserve all evidence of his use of Grok and other AI chatbots, including Gemini, Perplexity and ChatGPT, in carrying out official duties. The letter, first reported by Politico, asks whether he has solicited advice from such systems on constitutional responsibilities including waging war and the operation to remove Nicolás Maduro from Venezuela.

Pentagon has obligated almost all of its One Big Beautiful Bill funding

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Defense Department said it has obligated 97.5% of the $152.4 billion authorised under the One Big Beautiful Bill, or $148.6 billion, according to Military.com. The Navy obligated $48.7 billion of its $49.2 billion share. The Pentagon is seeking additional money from Congress as the cost of the Iran war has passed $47 billion.

Utah data center project refiles for 558 million gallons of water a year

tags: climate, tech
sources: @carolinegleich

A data center project backed by Kevin O'Leary has refiled an application for Utah water rights, seeking up to 558 million gallons a year from a ranch spring to supply gas plants and a 7.5 gigawatt data center next to the Great Salt Lake. Opponents note that Utah is one of the driest states and that a falling lake level exposes lakebed dust containing arsenic and heavy metals, breathed by 2.5 million people. A previous version of the application was withdrawn after a state-record 3,800 protests were filed last spring. Protests against application a55167 can be filed with the Division of Water Rights for $15, or a free letter of concern submitted, with a deadline of Nov. 4.

Medical professionals urge Missouri voters to reject Amendment 3

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

Hundreds of medical professionals are urging Missouri residents to vote against Amendment 3 on the November ballot, saying it would roll back reproductive rights the state's voters previously approved. The earlier Right to Reproductive Freedom Amendment guaranteed access to miscarriage and abortion care, birth control, safe birthing conditions and maternal health care. Supporters of that measure say state politicians are now seeking to reverse those protections and make access harder.

Ramaswamy pulls ad about Dr. Amy Acton's mother after backlash

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Vivek Ramaswamy has taken off air an advertisement concerning the mother of Dr. Amy Acton, his opponent in the Ohio governor's race, following significant public backlash. Some Ohio voters have said they are switching their support from Ramaswamy to Acton because of the ad.

Vance withdraws from Minnesota fraud announcement

tags: politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Vice President JD Vance cancelled his appearance at a news conference on fraud in St. Cloud, Minnesota, with the announcement made late Thursday and no explanation given, according to USA Today. The event is still scheduled to go ahead, with FBI Director Kash Patel, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz and FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson making the administration's announcement on its anti-fraud efforts.

Harris advises against impeachment route if Democrats win Congress

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Asked what she would recommend to congressional leadership if Democrats win the House and Senate next week, former Vice President Kamala Harris said going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, and instead suggested pursuing policy legislation that would force a presidential veto. The remarks drew criticism from commentators who argue that investigations and impeachment proceedings should be pursued regardless of whether there are votes to convict. Critics also noted that the International Criminal Court has no jurisdiction over the United States because successive presidents, beginning with Bill Clinton, did not sign the Rome Statute.

Trump tells South Carolina rally that poor Americans are doing better than ever

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

At a rally in South Carolina five days before Election Day, President Trump said that Black and Jewish Americans who vote Democratic are crazy, repeating a line he has used before and adding that they are crazy anyway. He claimed poverty figures showed poor people are doing better than they have ever done, and called for an investigation into negative polling by the state's next governor. He also referred to a hurricane as a water cane on the grounds that it had more water than anybody.

Vance deflects question on housing costs at Texas event

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Asked by a young attendee how the right expects his generation to start families when the average American home costs more than $415,000, Vice President JD Vance opened his answer by noting that of the four or five questions he had received, only one had been about a senator's appearance, a question posed by Fox host Jesse Watters. He went on to address affordability after the aside. The questioner had argued that the cost of home ownership and of raising a family disincentivises the early marriage and childbearing the right encourages.

Palestinian landowner arrested after settler dispute during olive harvest

tags: legal, war
sources: @total.hypocrisy

In the occupied West Bank, an Israeli shepherd brought his herd onto land belonging to a Palestinian who was harvesting olives and allowed the animals to feed off the trees. An argument followed and the military, local police and security forces arrived; the Palestinian landowner was the one arrested despite being the victim of the incident. Palestinians in the occupied West Bank are subject to military law and have almost no recourse when the military intervenes, and footage of the encounter was provided to the landowner's lawyers. His condition is unknown after the southern region was locked down following an attack there.

Three arrested over Athens blast that killed six including four Americans

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Greek authorities arrested two Greek men and an Albanian national over a Sept. 25 explosion in the Plaka district of Athens that killed six people, among them four Americans. The suspects are accused of stealing copper gas pipes from the building, which investigators say damaged the gas supply and caused a leak. The blast was triggered when a resident switched on a light. The three are due before a prosecutor Friday.

Trump posts meme saying Jesus sent him to reverse Obama's policies

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump posted a meme on Truth Social suggesting that Jesus sent him to reverse all of Obama's policies, on the premise that Obama had reversed those of Jesus. It is the latest instance of the president invoking religious imagery on the platform to promote himself.
